questions.text: A 200 mm thick concrete slab has a construction joint. What is the minimum steel area required for temporary/shrinkage reinforcement across 1 meter width of the joint (fy = 420 MPa, Grade 60)?

options.text: 200 mm²
360 mm²
500 mm²
400 mm²

rationale.d: 400 mm² is close but not exact (0.002 × 1000 × 200).
rationale.correct: Temporary/shrinkage reinforcement at construction joints requires ρ_temp = 0.0018 (NSCP 6.4.2, for Grade 60 steel). Steel area = ρ × b × h = 0.0018 × 1000 mm × 200 mm = 360 mm² for 1 m width.
rationale.takeaway: Review the correct answer and associated code provision.

questions.text: A floor construction joint is located 2.8 m from one support in a 7 m span girder. The girder is 500 mm wide. What is the minimum offset distance from this floor joint to place the girder's construction joint per NSCP?

options.text: 500 mm

rationale.a: 500 mm = 1× beam width only — the code requires 2× beam width minimum offset.
rationale.c: 2000 mm = 4× beam width — exceeds the minimum requirement. The minimum is 2× beam width = 1000 mm.
rationale.d: 1400 mm is an arbitrary value with no code basis. The offset is calculated as 2 × beam width.
rationale.correct: NSCP 6.4.1 requires the girder construction joint to be offset at least 2× the width of the intersecting beam. For a 500 mm wide girder: 2 × 500 = 1000 mm minimum offset from the floor joint location.
rationale.takeaway: Girder construction joint offset = 2 × beam width. For a 500 mm beam, the minimum offset is 1000 mm.

questions.text: A 250 mm beam at a construction joint requires temporary shrinkage steel. For a 3 m length of beam, what is the total steel area (A_s) required for 1 m width of the joint, using fy = 420 MPa (Grade 60)?

options.text: 450 mm²
500 mm²
600 mm²
750 mm²

rationale.correct: Temp/shrinkage steel area = ρ × b × h = 0.0018 × 1000 mm × 250 mm = 450 mm² for 1 m width of joint (NSCP 6.4.2). The beam length (3 m) does not affect this calculation; it is area per unit width of joint.
rationale.takeaway: Review the correct answer and associated code provision.

questions.text: A one-way floor slab spans 6 meters between supports. Per NSCP, within which region must a construction joint be located to minimize flexural stress?

options.text: 0 to 2 meters from support, which is typically avoided to prevent stress concentration
2 to 4 meters from support (middle third)
4 to 6 meters from support, which may lead to increased flexural stress
Exactly at 3 meters (center), which is not recommended due to potential stress issues

rationale.a: 0–2 m is the end third, near the support where moment and shear are high.
rationale.c: 4–6 m is the other end third, also near support with high stresses.
rationale.d: The center (3 m) is within the middle third (2–4 m) but the entire region 2–4 m is acceptable.
rationale.correct: Construction joints for continuous or simply supported slabs must be located within the middle third of the span (NSCP 6.4.1). For a 6 m span, the middle third spans from 2 m to 4 m from support. Bending moment is lowest in this region.
rationale.takeaway: Review the correct answer and associated code provision.

questions.text: For a 180 mm thick slab at a construction joint, what is the maximum spacing of temporary shrinkage reinforcement bars per NSCP?

options.text: 900 mm
450 mm
600 mm
360 mm

rationale.a: 900 mm = 5h but exceeds the 450 mm absolute maximum.
rationale.c: 600 mm is between 450 mm and 900 mm but is not the code value.
rationale.d: 360 mm is more restrictive than required.
rationale.correct: Maximum spacing = min(5h, 450 mm) where h = slab thickness (NSCP 6.4.2). For 180 mm slab: min(5 × 180, 450) = min(900, 450) = 450 mm. The 450 mm cap governs.
rationale.takeaway: Review the correct answer and associated code provision.

questions.code_citation: NSCP 2015 § 6.4.2 (Temp Steel Spacing — max 5h or 450 mm)

questions.text: At a construction joint between a beam and a column in a moment frame, what is the minimum percentage of the beam's primary flexural reinforcement that must be continued across the joint as dowels?

rationale.a: 25% is insufficient for adequate shear transfer in moment-frame joints.
rationale.d: 100% is overly conservative; 50% is the code minimum.
rationale.correct: At construction joints at beam-column intersections, aAll primary flexural reinforcement must be properly developed/anchored through the joint per detailing requirements (NSCP 2015 §12.12 for development lengths; no specific % dowel requirement at construction joints)to ensure rigid shear transfer (NSCP 6.4.2, ACI 318-19 § 6.5.3).
rationale.takeaway: Review the correct answer and associated code provision.

questions.text: A construction joint in a floor slab is detailed with temp steel bars spaced at 600 mm center-to-center. The slab is 150 mm thick. Is this spacing compliant per NSCP?

options.text: Yes, compliant; spacing is within 5h = 750 mm, which is the maximum allowable spacing for this slab thickness
No, non-compliant; maximum allowed spacing is 450 mm (cap overrules 5h).
Yes, compliant; 600 mm < 750 mm, which is within the allowable range for this application
No, non-compliant; spacing must be < 300 mm for all slabs, which is a stricter interpretation

rationale.a: While 5h = 750 mm, the 450 mm cap is the controlling criterion.
rationale.c: 600 mm > 450 mm, so it violates the spacing limit.
rationale.d: 300 mm is more restrictive than required (but would be acceptable as conservative design).
rationale.correct: Maximum spacing = min(5h, 450 mm) = min(750, 450) = 450 mm (NSCP 6.4.2). The 450 mm absolute cap governs. Specified 600 mm exceeds this limit and is non-compliant. Bars must be tightened to ≤450 mm spacing.
rationale.takeaway: Review the correct answer and associated code provision.

questions.text: Before pouring concrete at a construction joint, the existing concrete surface must be treated per NSCP. Which action is correct?

options.text: Seal the surface with epoxy to prevent water infiltration and ensure long-term durability of the joint
Remove laitance and expose aggregate; saturate with water (but no free standing water).
Leave the surface as-is; bonding agent will handle adhesion, which simplifies the preparation process
Use a power washer and dry completely before the new pour to remove debris and ensure a clean bonding surface

rationale.a: Epoxy sealing is not the standard method; it can interfere with concrete bonding.
rationale.c: Leaving the surface untreated compromises bond; laitance is a weak layer.
rationale.d: Complete drying prevents hydration of the new concrete at the interface. The surface should be moist (SSD), not dry.
rationale.correct: Construction joint surface preparation per NSCP 6.4.3: (1) remove laitance by light chipping or grinding to expose aggregate, (2) saturate the surface with water but remove excess free water (SSD condition), and (3) optionally apply bonding agent if desired (NSCP permits but does not require it). This maximizes mechanical interlock and bond between old and new concrete.
rationale.takeaway: Review the correct answer and associated code provision.

questions.text: A 4 m clear span floor slab requires a construction joint. The architect proposes placement at 3.5 m from one support. Is this compliant with NSCP location requirements?

options.text: Yes, compliant; 3.5 m is within the span.
No, non-compliant; joint is outside the middle third (1.33–2.67 m from support).
Yes, compliant; any location away from supports is acceptable.
No, must be placed exactly at 2 m (center of span).

rationale.a: Compliance requires the joint to be within the middle third, not just anywhere in the span.
rationale.c: Not any location is acceptable; middle third is required.
rationale.d: The joint does not have to be at the exact center; anywhere in the middle third (1.33–2.67 m) is acceptable.
rationale.correct: For a 4 m span, the middle third = 4/3 ≈ 1.33 m at each end, so the valid region is 1.33–2.67 m from one support (NSCP 6.4.1). The proposed 3.5 m location is in the outer third (beyond 2.67 m), where moment is higher. This is non-compliant.
rationale.takeaway: Review the correct answer and associated code provision.

questions.text: A construction joint in a slab is detailed with temporary steel bars running perpendicular to the joint (i.e., crossing the joint). Is this detailing correct per NSCP?

options.text: Yes, perpendicular bars are correct for shear transfer across the joint, ensuring structural integrity
No, temp steel must run parallel to the joint, normal to the shear flow direction (NSCP 6.4.2).
Yes, either parallel or perpendicular is acceptable, depending on the specific load conditions
No, no reinforcement is required at construction joints, as they are designed to accommodate movement

rationale.a: Perpendicular bars serve as dowels, not as temp/shrinkage steel (different purpose).
rationale.c: The orientation is not interchangeable; the standard is parallel to the joint.
rationale.d: Reinforcement is required: temp steel (parallel) and often dowels (perpendicular) for shear.
rationale.correct: Temporary/shrinkage reinforcement at construction joints must be placed parallel to the joint, oriented normal to the principal shear flow direction (NSCP 6.4.2). This configuration resTemporary/shrinkage reinforcement must be placed perpendicular to the joint (crossing it) to control cracking (consistent with ACI 318/NSCP shrinkage & temp reinforcement orientation)for rigid shear transfer.
rationale.takeaway: Review the correct answer and associated code provision.

questions.code_citation: NSCP 2015 § 6.4.2 (Temp Steel Orientation — parallel to joint)
